data.heading: The digestive system
data.text: The role of the digestive system is to break down food into nutrients that the body can use.
The digestive system also helps in getting rid of the undigested part of the food from the body.
The digestive system contains an 8m long tract called the digestive tract.
The saliva in the mouth mixes with food and starts to break it down so that it becomes easier to swallow it.
The swallowed food then travels down a long tube called the oesophagus, to the stomach.
The oesophagus is about 25 cm long in a human adult.
The gastric juices in the stomach break the food down further into a paste.
The small intestine is the longest part of the digestive system. It is about 5 metres long.
The nourishing part of the food goes into the bloodstream from the small intestine and is transported all over the body.
The large intestine removes excess water and salts from the undigested food.
The remaining part of the undigested food travels through the rectum and comes out of the body through the anus.
